game: CHI @ GB, Week 5 2026 (morning of kickoff; spread/total/weather/inactives not saved)

script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is treated as a competitive divisional game at Green Bay with no blowout flag and no priced team totals. Chicago's backfield loses Kyle Monangai (50 carries, 224 yards in weeks 2-4), so the base lean is D'Andre Swift as the lead runner against a Green Bay front allowing 4.39 YPC and 11 runs of 10+. Green Bay's own run game is a thin committee (Kaleb Johnson 20/80, Marshawn Lloyd 17/44, Chris Brooks out) behind Aaron Banks and Jacob Monk doubtful, so Jordan Love still throws, but Chicago blitzes 40% and Green Bay's EPA/dropback is -0.22 vs the blitz versus +0.20 with no blitz, which compresses the pass game toward short/middle (Tucker Kraft, backs) and away from Matthew Golden's 14.7-yard average depth of target.
script.flip1: Caleb Williams (questionable, hamstring) sits or is a non-factor, Tyson Bagent plays, and Chicago falls behind. The Swift carry spike never shows up because the script goes pass-heavy; Chicago WR overs die with the QB change, and Bagent's 11.5 rush line is the live QB-run prop instead. Green Bay can then lean on a clock-killing run that their banged-up line may not actually execute.
script.flip2: Williams is full go, the patchwork Green Bay line holds the blitz, and it becomes a vertical game. Golden (week-4 21 but weeks of 95 and 100) and Christian Watson (147, 41, 96, 47) clear, Chicago has to throw, and Swift's rush line stalls the way a chase or shootout stalls a back. That flip cashes correlated pass overs together and loses a trench stack.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, MOFO/MOFC, or man/zone rate is in the pack (step 4 limited). What is saved is location YPA. Green Bay's pass defense is balanced: left 6.78 (46 throws), middle 6.95 (19), right 7.02 (51), with only 6 passes of 20+ for 126 yards in four games. Chicago's shell bleeds the middle: 10.9 YPA on 20 middle throws, versus left 6.44 (41) and right 7.74 (38), and they have allowed more explosives (9 passes of 20+ / 109 yards).
matchup.pressure: Both teams blitz 40%. Chicago's offense is fine against pressure (EPA/dropback +0.25 vs blitz, +0.20 vs none), so this is not a Chicago checkdown game. Green Bay is the pressure problem: EPA/dropback -0.22 vs blitz and +0.20 with no blitz, in front of an OL with Banks and Monk doubtful. Pressure that gets home should cut deep WR yards and lift RB/TE catches. Counter: Chicago DE Shemar Turner is questionable, so the blitz may not arrive.
matchup.bleeds: Green Bay run defense allows 4.39 YPC and 11 runs of 10+ — leaky enough to support a workhorse, not a collapse. Chicago run defense is softer at 4.94 YPC and 10 runs of 10+, but Green Bay's backs are inefficient (Lloyd 2.59 YPC) and the OL is doubtful, so the bleed is not a clean GB RB over. Chicago's real bleed is the middle (10.9 YPA). They also give up more 20+ passes than Green Bay, which cuts against fading Green Bay's deep shots on coverage alone.
matchup.overlap: The overlap the pack actually supports is Green Bay's short/middle usage into Chicago's middle bleed and missing LB (Elliott out, Sewell questionable): Kraft is 18 targets at 2.7 air yards per target (83 yards, 4.6 yards per target), not Golden. Golden is the anti-overlap: 25 targets, 368 air yards, 14.7 aDOT, which is what a 40% blitz and a bad blitz-EPA quarterback are supposed to kill, except Chicago has allowed 9 explosives and Turner may not play. Chicago's primary pass options (Burden 24 targets, Odunze 17 targets / 215 air yards) do not face a Green Bay zone hole; Green Bay's YPA is ~7.0 sideline to sideline. The run overlap is Swift into 4.39 YPC with Hargrave questionable, after Monangai's 50 carries leave.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Swift over 84.5 lost. The market had already lifted the number from a 62-yard split-backfield average to 84.5, and the prior was right: weeks 2-4 were 45, 84, and 58. Chicago did not get a positive run script — Williams' hamstring either knocked him out or the game flipped early — so the vacated Monangai carries became pass attempts and a few Roschon touches, not 22 Swift carries. Hargrave played, Green Bay knew the run was coming, and 3.67 YPC on a telegraphed plan never got the matchup bump to 4.39. The same Monday, a Golden under would also have been the wrong force: he had already cleared 57.5 in three of four games, Chicago's secondary had been giving up explosives, and Turner was the questionable pass rusher the under needed. That counter is why Golden is not on the slip.
slip_story: One story only: trench game, Chicago runs it through Swift after Monangai, Green Bay's vertical game is the part that should suffer if the blitz and the OL injuries show up. Swift rush over is the only allowed-market leg that survived the pre-mortem. Do not add Chicago pass overs (Williams questionable; Odunze/Raymond/Burden need him) or Green Bay deep overs (Golden, Watson), which need the shootout flip. Kraft over would be the correlated short-area piece but the 49.5 rung is too far above 27.7 L3 yards to join. Golden under was the correlated pressure piece and was dropped because the counter-case was stronger. House shape would want 3-4 same-script legs and no TDs; this pack does not have a second legal leg, so the slip stays one leg until inactives and a real number. No stake.
